title: POE: macOS/Xcode-inspired UI redesign
description: Replace brutalist black-border aesthetic with polished macOS app design: system font, sidebar navigation (Xcode-style), subtle borders/shadows, light + dark mode via CSS custom properties and data-theme attribute.

title: POE: End-to-end resolution flow
description: Wire the full loop: human resolves a queue item → decision recorded as DAG node → awakeable completed → agent receives answer on stdin and resumes. Full audit trail in the project DAG.
design: On resolve: (1) create Decision node in SQLite dag.db linked to triggering queue item via approved-by edge, (2) call Restate resolveItem to complete awakeable, (3) send chosen option JSON to agent stdin via PTY, (4) update queue_item status to resolved, (5) emit dag:node:upserted for the new Decision node. Agent resumes from the decision point with the human's answer in context.
close_reason: Full resolution loop implemented: queue_items schema, create/list/resolve commands, Restate awakeable completion, Decision DAG node, queue events, QueueView UI with option cards. PTY stdin stub in place for bp6-2a5.1.

title: POE: Queue view UI
description: Build the queue view as POE's primary UI surface. Ordered list of pending queue items with full context. Human resolves items inline; resolved items drop off the queue.
design: Primary panel, always visible. Each item renders: agent identity, question, options as clickable cards, context snapshot as collapsible DAG subgraph. Actions: choose option (resolve), dismiss, stop agent. Subscribes to queue:item:added (append to list) and queue:item:resolved (remove from list) Tauri events. Empty state: 'No decisions pending — agents are running.' Ordered by priority then created_at.
close_reason: QueueView redesigned: renders pending QueueItems from queueItemsListAtom, clickable option cards invoke resolve_queue_item, subscribes to queue:item:added + queue:item:resolved via useDagEvents, empty state message included

title: POE: Restate queue service
description: Implement the Restate virtual object that manages queue items. Handles creation with an awakeable, listing pending items per project, and resolution that unblocks the suspended workflow.
design: Restate virtual object keyed by project_id. Handlers: createItem(item) → stores item, returns awakeable_id; resolveItem(id, resolution) → completes awakeable, updates status; listPending() → returns items sorted by priority. On createItem: write to SQLite queue_items, emit queue:item:added Tauri event. On resolveItem: complete Restate awakeable, write resolution to SQLite, emit queue:item:resolved.
close_reason: Axum queue service on port 9082: createItem/resolveItem/listPending HTTP handlers, Restate awakeable integration, auto-registration on startup

title: POE: Queue item schema
description: Define the QueueItem data contract used by agents, Restate, and the UI. SQLite table and Restate virtual object state shape. This is the shared schema everything in Phase 2 depends on.
design: SQLite: queue_items(id, project_id, agent_id, workflow_id, awakeable_id, question TEXT, options JSON, context_snapshot JSON, priority INT, status TEXT, created_at, resolved_at, resolution JSON). Status enum: pending|resolved|dismissed. Restate virtual object state mirrors this minus context_snapshot (too large for K/V). Context snapshot = serialized DAG subgraph (N hops from triggering node).
close_reason: Schema fully implemented: queue_items SQLite migration (v2), QueueItem/QueueItemOption/NewQueueItem Rust types, TypeScript QueueItem/QueueItemOption/QueueItemStatus types in types.ts

title: POE: Agent decision protocol
description: Define and implement the protocol by which agents raise decision points to the orchestrator. Agents emit structured JSON-lines on stdout; Rust PTY layer intercepts and forwards to Restate queue service.
design: Agent emits to stdout: {type:'poe:decision', question:string, options:[{id,label,description}], context:{nodeId?, rationale?}, priority:0-3}. Rust PTY parser: scan stdout lines for poe: prefix, deserialise, call Restate queue service via HTTP, write queue item to SQLite, pass non-poe lines through to UI as normal agent output. Agent then blocks waiting for stdin response. Resolution sends {decision_id, chosen_option} to agent stdin.
close_reason: PTY agent spawning + poe:decision stdout protocol + write_to_agent stdin implemented in agents.rs

title: POE: Project open/close UI
description: Basic project management: open a directory, initialise or open its .poe/dag.db, hold project context in the UI. Empty state when no project is open.
design: Tauri dialog plugin for directory picker. On open: Rust opens/creates {dir}/.poe/dag.db, runs migrations, loads project node, emits initial state snapshot to frontend. Project context in Tauri managed state. Frontend: empty state with open-project CTA, project header showing name once open. Close: flush writes, close SQLite connection, clear frontend state.

title: POE: Reactive event bridge
description: Wire SQLite writes to push typed Tauri events to the frontend as deltas. No polling, no full reloads. Frontend subscribes to events and applies changes in place.
design: Rust: after each DAG write, call app.emit() with typed event + delta payload. Events: dag:node:upserted {node}, dag:node:deleted {id}, dag:edge:upserted {edge}, dag:edge:deleted {id}, queue:item:added {item}, queue:item:resolved {id}, workflow:status {workflowId, status}. Frontend: useEffect listeners per event type, update Zustand/Jotai store in place. Initial load = single SQL query; subsequent updates = events only.

title: POE: Restate sidecar lifecycle
description: Bundle the Restate server binary with POE. Spawn it as a child process on app launch, verify it is healthy before proceeding, and kill it cleanly on app exit.
design: Download restate-server binary at build time (build.rs or tauri beforeBuildCommand). Spawn via std::process::Command, capture stdout/stderr. Health check: poll http://localhost:9070/health until ready (max 10s). Store child handle in Tauri managed state. On app exit hook: send SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL if needed. Config: ports 9070 (admin) and 9080 (services) on localhost only.

title: POE: SQLite DAG store
description: Implement the per-project SQLite DAG store. Schema with typed nodes and semantic edges. Rust CRUD layer. Project open/close creates or opens {project}/.poe/dag.db.
design: Crate: rusqlite with bundled feature. Schema: nodes(id TEXT PK, type TEXT, project_id TEXT, data TEXT/JSON, created_at, updated_at), edges(id TEXT PK, from_id TEXT, to_id TEXT, type TEXT, data TEXT, created_at). Node types enum: Project|Epic|Feature|Task|Decision|KnowledgeArtifact|AgentOutput|Review. Edge types: blocks|depends-on|generated-by|approved-by|discovered-from|implements|tests|contradicts. Migrations table for schema versioning. WAL mode enabled on open.

title: POE: Tauri app scaffold
description: Create a fresh Tauri + React app in poe/ alongside bp6. App should build and run independently. Establish build scripts that work alongside bp6 in the same repo.
design: Use create-tauri-app in toolkit/bp6/poe/. React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind (same stack as bp6). Basic window with placeholder queue view. Build script at poe/build_run.sh mirroring bp6's. No beads dependency.

title: POE Phase 2: Human Queue
description: Build the queue view as POE's primary UI surface. Implement Restate awakeable-based workflow suspension for agent decision points. Queue items carry full DAG context. Human resolves items; agents unblock and resume.
design: Queue item = Restate virtual object keyed by (project_id, item_id). Each item holds: question, options, context snapshot (DAG subgraph), awakeable_id, priority, agent_id. UI: ordered list, full context inline, resolve/redirect/stop actions. Tauri event: queue:item:added, queue:item:resolved. Agents raise decisions via local HTTP to Restate; Restate suspends workflow; resolution unblocks via awakeable.

title: POE Phase 1: Foundation
description: Scaffold the POE Tauri app in poe/ alongside bp6. Establish the SQLite DAG store with typed nodes and semantic edges. Manage Restate sidecar lifecycle. Wire the reactive bridge so SQLite writes emit Tauri events to the frontend.
design: New Tauri app at toolkit/bp6/poe/. SQLite schema: nodes(id, type, project_id, data jsonb, created_at, updated_at), edges(id, from_id, to_id, type, data jsonb). Node types: Project|Epic|Feature|Task|Decision|KnowledgeArtifact|AgentOutput|Review. Edge types: blocks|depends-on|generated-by|approved-by|discovered-from|implements|tests|contradicts. Restate spawned as child process on app launch, killed on exit, state in app data dir.

title: Pairti Orchestration Engine (POE)
description: bp6 has proven the visualization model but diverges from the end goal: a local-first AI orchestration IDE where agents run the V-lifecycle and humans oversee via a work queue. POE is a fresh Tauri app built alongside bp6 in the same repo, replacing beads with a SQLite DAG, adding Restate for durable workflow orchestration, and inverting the IDE model — queue-first, not file-tree-first.
design: Stack: Tauri + React (same as bp6) + Restate sidecar (local RocksDB) + SQLite WAL per project. Split: Restate owns workflow execution state and human queue (awakeables); SQLite owns DAG nodes/edges/knowledge/artifacts. Reactive bridge: Rust writes SQLite → emits Tauri events with deltas → frontend applies in place. No JSONL, no polling. Borrows from bp6: PTY session management, Tauri IPC patterns, DAG algorithms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Human queue surfaces all pending agent decisions; no manual checking required
- Agents run concurrently across multiple open projects
- All project state lives in {project}/.poe/dag.db — portable, no central store
- UI updates are event-driven deltas; no full reloads
- bp6 continues to run untouched during POE development

title: POE: Fix watchdog liveness — remove AgentHandle from registry on PTY EOF
description: The 7fi.1 watchdog uses Arc::strong_count to detect agent exit, but PTY EOF never removes the AgentHandle from the AgentState registry map. The strong count never drops to 1 so the watchdog runs forever for crashed/completed agents. Fix: in the PTY reader thread, after the BufReader lines loop exits (EOF), remove the agent_id from the AgentState handles map. This naturally drops the AgentHandle's Arc references, the strong count falls to 1, and the watchdog exits on its next poll. Also ensures the registry does not leak handles for finished agents.

title: POE: Claude session ID tracking and resume on respawn
description: Generate a UUID when a workflow is created and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude at spawn time. Store the UUID in WorkflowRecord (schema v5: session_id TEXT column). On respawn after crash or decision, use --resume <uuid> instead of rebuilding the prompt. Replace auto_continue in project.rs (which prepends resolution text to a fresh prompt) with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write the resolution JSON to agent stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. Reference: bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs and session.rs for the --session-id / --resume pattern.
design:
Session ID tracking is a prerequisite for durable agent resumption. Design principles:

1. GENERATE AT SPAWN: When a workflow is created, generate a UUID and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude. Do not attempt to parse session ID from PTY output. The ID is known before the process starts and stored immediately.

2. SCHEMA: Add session_id TEXT column to the workflows table (schema migration v5). Populated at workflow creation time, never null for claude-backed workflows.

3. REPLACE auto_continue_workflow: The current auto_continue_workflow in project.rs rebuilds the prompt and spawns a fresh claude process. Replace this with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write resolution context to stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. No new child workflow record needed for linear continuations — update the existing workflow status back to running and respawn in-place.

4. HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE: spawn_agent_internal is called from project.rs (Tauri command) today. As we move toward Restate-driven orchestration, the spawn logic must not depend on Tauri app state. The session_id should be passed into the spawn call, not derived from Tauri state inside the function. Design the interface so it could be called from a standalone Axum handler with no Tauri dependency.

5. REFERENCE: bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs for --session-id / --resume flag pattern. bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/session_index.rs for persistence pattern.
notes: Implemented: schema v5 (session_id TEXT on workflows), NewWorkflow.session_id, WorkflowRecord.session_id, SpawnAgentParams.session_id + resume bool, --session-id injection on initial spawn, --resume injection on continuation, replaced auto_continue_workflow with resume_workflow (no child record, no fan-in pollution), fixed watchdog liveness bug (remove AgentHandle on PTY EOF). Tests: 3/3 pass.

title: POE: Durable workflow execution — session IDs + Restate registration
description: Full crash-safe workflow orchestration. Two parts: (1) Claude session ID tracking so agents can resume mid-conversation after a crash or restart — generate UUID at spawn, pass --session-id to claude, store in WorkflowRecord, use --resume on respawn; replace auto_continue prompt-rebuilding with session resume + stdin injection. (2) Register the queue service as a real Restate service endpoint using the Rust SDK, so workflow steps are durably journaled and replayed on restart — not just awakeable consumers.

title: POE: Wire poe:decision to awakeables so resolution unblocks agent
description: Currently poe:decision from PTY creates a queue item but does NOT create a Restate awakeable, so when the human resolves the decision the agent's stdin is not notified. Need to: create an awakeable when poe:decision arrives, store awakeable_id in the queue item, resolve the awakeable on human decision, and write the resolution JSON to agent stdin via the PTY writer. This closes the human-in-the-loop feedback loop.
close_reason: Implemented: handle_poe_decision now creates Restate awakeable and stores ID in queue item; handle_resolve_item writes resolution JSON to agent PTY stdin via write_to_workflow_agent

title: POE: Project launcher with recents and favourites
description: Replace the bare Open Project button with a proper launcher screen showing favourite projects, last N recent projects, and an Open button. Opening a blank directory creates a new project naturally.

title: POE: Embed Restate admin panel as tab in UI
description: Add a Restate tab to the POE app that embeds the Restate admin panel (http://localhost:9070) in an iframe. Gives developers direct access to Restate's built-in UI without leaving POE.
close_reason: Implemented tab bar in App.tsx + RestateView.tsx iframe embedding http://localhost:9070

title: POE: Provenance traversal
description: Full lineage view for any DAG node. Traverse incoming and outgoing edges to understand why something was built the way it was: what decisions, what agents, what prior knowledge shaped this artifact.
design: Triggered from any node in the Gantt or probe panel. Provenance panel: renders the local subgraph N hops from the selected node as a force-directed or hierarchical graph. Edge labels show semantic type (generated-by, approved-by, discovered-from, etc.). Click any node in the provenance graph to navigate to it. Depth slider: 1–5 hops. SQL: recursive CTE walking edges table from seed node. Highlights: human decision nodes (amber), agent output nodes (blue), knowledge artifacts (green). Answers the question: why does this exist?

title: POE: Stop & redirect controls
description: Human intervention controls on running workflows. Stop terminates the agent and cancels the workflow cleanly. Redirect injects a correction instruction into the running agent and records it as a Decision node in the DAG.
design: Stop: (1) SIGTERM agent PTY, (2) cancel Restate workflow, (3) update DAG node status to cancelled, (4) create Decision node linked via approved-by with reason. Redirect: (1) human types correction instruction in probe panel, (2) write Redirect Decision node to DAG (approved-by edge to workflow node), (3) inject instruction to agent stdin via PTY, (4) update Restate workflow metadata with redirect count. Both actions available from probe panel (F3) and agent activity panel (F2). Redirect is non-destructive — agent continues running with new context.

title: POE: Probe & inspect
description: Deep inspection of any running workflow or DAG node. Human can see the full context the agent is operating in: DAG subgraph, decision history, artifacts produced so far, current Restate workflow step and state.
design: Triggered by clicking a Gantt bar (F1) or agent panel (F2). Probe panel shows: (1) DAG node detail — title, description, all linked edges with their targets; (2) Workflow state — current Restate step, step history, pending awakeables; (3) Decision history — all Decision nodes generated-by this workflow, with human resolutions; (4) Artifacts — all AgentOutput nodes produced so far with content preview. Data fetched from SQLite on demand (not event-driven — point-in-time snapshot). Refresh button for live re-fetch.

title: POE: Agent activity view
description: Per-agent real-time view of what each running agent is doing. Shows current workflow step, live stdout stream, which DAG node it is working on, and elapsed time. One panel per active agent.
design: Subscribes to workflow:status events for agent list. Per agent: stream PTY stdout to frontend via Tauri event (agent:stdout {workflowId, line}) — non-poe lines only, protocol events are consumed by Rust. Display: agent identity + assigned DAG node, current step label (from poe:step events), scrolling stdout, elapsed time, status badge. Multi-agent: tabbed or stacked panels. Selecting an agent panel feeds the probe view (F3).

title: POE: Live DAG / Gantt view
description: SQLite-backed Gantt chart showing the project DAG in real-time. Workflow execution status overlaid on nodes. Updates reactively via Tauri events. Borrows DAG layout algorithms from bp6 but reads from dag.db not JSONL.
design: Port topological sort and critical path algorithms from bp6 lib.rs. Query SQLite for nodes/edges on project open, build in-memory graph, render WBS + Gantt. Overlay workflow status on bars: running (animated), suspended/awaiting-human (amber), failed (red), completed (green). Live updates: dag:node:upserted events patch the in-memory graph and re-render affected rows only — no full reload. Gantt is secondary view, always visible alongside the queue. Click a bar → triggers probe (F3).

title: POE: Work assignment
description: Human selects a DAG node and assigns it to the orchestrator. POE determines the appropriate workflow type, creates the Restate workflow, spawns the agent, and links everything back to the DAG node.
design: UI: right-click (or action button) on any open DAG node → 'Assign to agent'. POE infers workflow type from node type (Feature → ImplementationWorkflow, etc.) or human picks from dropdown. Rust Tauri command: createWorkflow(nodeId, workflowType, config) → calls Restate to start workflow → spawns PTY agent with system prompt constructed from DAG node data + context subgraph → updates DAG node status to in_progress → emits dag:node:upserted. Config: model, max_steps, agent_rig.

title: POE: Sub-workflow orchestration
description: Parent workflows spawn child workflows for sub-items (e.g. a Feature workflow fans out into Task workflows). Parent waits on all children to complete before proceeding. Handles partial failure.
design: Restate fan-out pattern: parent workflow calls ctx.run(() => restateClient.send(ChildWorkflow, nodeId)) for each child DAG node. Fan-in: parent awaits all child workflow IDs via Promise.all equivalent in Restate. Partial failure policy: if any child fails, parent suspends and raises queue item asking human whether to retry, skip, or abort. DAG: child workflow nodes linked to parent via implements edge. Progress rolls up: parent node status derived from child completion ratio.

title: POE: Agent progress protocol
description: Extend the Phase 2 JSON-lines stdout protocol with progress events. Agents report step transitions, artifact creation, and workflow completion. Rust PTY parser forwards these to Restate and the DAG.
design: Extends poe: prefix protocol from Phase 2. New event types: {type:'poe:step', step:string, status:'started'|'completed'|'failed', detail?:string} — updates workflow step in Restate; {type:'poe:artifact', kind:'code'|'doc'|'test'|'decision', nodeId?:string, content:string} — creates AgentOutput node in SQLite DAG linked to current workflow node via generated-by edge; {type:'poe:done', summary:string} — signals workflow step complete, Restate advances to next step. Non-poe stdout lines pass through to session view as before.

title: POE: Agent spawn & lifecycle
description: Orchestrator spawns PTY sessions for agents and monitors them throughout their lifecycle. Handles heartbeat, crash detection, graceful stop, and forced kill. Ported and extended from bp6's session management.
design: Port bp6 src-tauri/src/agent/pty.rs as starting point. Extend with: orchestrator-managed spawn (workflow_id + node_id attached to session metadata), heartbeat via periodic stdout ping/pong, crash detection (PTY exit → notify Restate workflow → mark workflow failed), graceful stop (SIGTERM → drain stdout → close PTY), forced kill (SIGKILL after timeout). Agent sessions stored in Tauri managed state keyed by workflow_id. Emit workflow:status Tauri events on lifecycle transitions.

title: POE: V-lifecycle workflow definitions
description: Define Restate workflow types for each phase of the V-lifecycle. Each workflow has durable steps, knows how to update the project DAG, and can raise decision points into the human queue.
design: Restate workflow types: RequirementsWorkflow, DesignWorkflow, ImplementationWorkflow, ValidationWorkflow, DeploymentWorkflow. Each follows the same interface: input is a DAG node ID (the work item); steps are durable ctx.run() blocks; each step can call ctx.awakeable() to raise a queue item. On step completion, workflow writes progress to SQLite dag.db (updates node status, creates AgentOutput nodes). Workflow state machine: pending → running → (suspended | failed | completed).

title: POE Phase 3: Workflow Engine
description: Define V-lifecycle workflow templates in Restate. Wire agent spawn/monitor via PTY sessions. Agents report progress and raise decision points. Sub-workflows spawn from parent (Feature spawns Task workflows).
design: Workflow types: RequirementsWorkflow, DesignWorkflow, ImplementationWorkflow, ValidationWorkflow, DeploymentWorkflow. Each is a Restate workflow with durable steps. Agents run in PTY sessions (ported from bp6). Agent protocol: structured stdout events (json lines) parsed by Rust, forwarded to Restate. Spawn model: human assigns work → Restate creates workflow → workflow spawns agent PTY → agent reports back.

title: POE Phase 4: Mission Control UI
description: Evolve the secondary view into a live mission control display. Gantt backed by SQLite DAG with real-time workflow status overlaid. Probe/inspect running agents. Stop and redirect controls. Full provenance traversal.
design: Gantt reads from SQLite directly (not Restate). Live updates via dag:node:updated events. Workflow status (running/paused/blocked) overlaid on bars. Click bar → agent output stream, current step, DAG context. Stop: Restate workflow cancellation + PTY kill. Redirect: inject new instruction into agent via PTY + update DAG node. Provenance: click any node → traverse incoming edges to root.

title: POE: Restate SDK service registration for poe-queue
description: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate to register poe-queue as a proper Restate service endpoint. Replace the placeholder /discover manifest (currently hardcoded, never registered) with the SDK-managed endpoint protocol. With handler isolation in place (bp6-pd9), handlers have no Tauri dependency and can be wired directly into the Restate SDK dispatcher. This makes workflow steps (spawn_agent, await_decision, fan_in, complete_workflow) durably journaled and replayed by Restate on restart.

title: POE: Handler isolation — remove AppHandle from queue_service Axum handlers
description: Remove Arc<AppHandle> from the Axum router state in queue_service.rs entirely. Replace with a purpose-built QueueServiceState struct containing a DagStore (or repository trait) and an mpsc::Sender<PoeEvent> for event emission. The Tauri host wires the receiver end to app.emit() via a background task. After this change, handler signatures contain no Tauri types and the module can compile and run without a Tauri dependency.

title: POE: Register queue service as Restate service endpoint
description: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate to register the POE queue service as a proper Restate service endpoint. Workflow steps (spawn agent, await decision, fan-in) become durable Restate handlers that Restate journals and replays on restart. The /discover endpoint in queue_service.rs is currently a placeholder — wire it up. With session IDs in place (7fi.4.1), a replayed spawn step passes --resume <session_id> so the agent continues mid-conversation. This is the piece that makes Restate actually do something beyond awakeable storage.
design:
Register POE as a real Restate service endpoint. This is the architectural centrepiece — not just a registration call, but establishing the handler isolation boundary that makes FaaS evolution possible.

VISION: Desktop today, FaaS eventually. Handlers must be written as if they are already stateless Lambda functions. Restate's journal and K/V store hold workflow state. Handlers are pure HTTP endpoints that read from DB / Restate state and emit results. No Tauri state inside handlers.

HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE (non-negotiable):
- Handlers MUST NOT call app.state::<ProjectState>() or any Tauri-specific API
- Handlers talk to SQLite (or future Supabase) directly via a db connection passed in at startup
- Handlers talk to Restate via the SDK — not via ad-hoc reqwest calls
- The handler Axum server should be extractable to a standalone binary with zero code changes

WHAT BECOMES A RESTATE HANDLER:
- spawn_workflow: durably spawn an agent for a workflow node. Restate journals this so on crash, the spawn is retried with --resume <session_id> (requires 7fi.4.1).
- await_decision: create an awakeable, store in queue item, suspend. Restate replays this correctly on restart — no more manual awakeable_id tracking.
- fan_in: durable join — Restate natively supports waiting for N child workflow completions.
- complete_workflow: mark node done, update DAG, trigger parent fan-in.

WHAT STAYS IN TAURI:
- UI state (open projects, selected node, etc.)
- PTY process management (spawning OS processes, reading stdout)
- Emitting Tauri events to the frontend
- Restate sidecar lifecycle (spawn/stop)

RESTATE SDK: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate. Do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol. The SDK handles framing, replay, and journal management.

STATE MIGRATION: Workflow state currently lives in SQLite embedded in Tauri. Handlers should access this via a repository interface (trait) so the backing store can be swapped to Supabase or Turso when moving to cloud without touching handler logic.

VISIBILITY PAYOFF: Once registered, the Restate admin panel at :9070 shows every workflow invocation, current step, retry history, and awakeable state. This replaces ad-hoc eprintln debugging and the JSONL dump pattern for workflow observability.

EVENT-DRIVEN PAYOFF: Handlers emit Restate events on state changes. The UI subscribes to these rather than polling SQLite. This eliminates the JSONL database dump pattern currently used for agent context injection.
notes:
Pre-implementation review findings that must be addressed in this task:

1. HANDLER ISOLATION VIOLATION — ALL HANDLERS: Every Axum handler in queue_service.rs takes State<Arc<AppHandle>> and accesses Tauri-managed state via app.state::<ProjectState>() and app.state::<AgentState>(). This is the core coupling that prevents standalone extraction. The AppHandle must be removed from Axum router state entirely. Replace with a purpose-built AppState struct containing: db connection (or DagStore), a channel/callback for emitting events to the UI, and any other handler dependencies. No Tauri types in handler signatures.

2. EVENT EMISSION DECOUPLING: Handlers currently emit Tauri events directly (app.emit(...)). In a standalone binary there is no Tauri. Replace with a thin EventSink trait (or mpsc sender) that the Tauri host wires to app.emit() and a standalone host wires to stdout/SSE/webhook. Handlers call event_sink.emit(event) — they do not know or care how it is delivered.

3. DISCOVER ENDPOINT IS A PLACEHOLDER: The /discover handler returns a hardcoded manifest with minProtocolVersion/maxProtocolVersion = 1 and is never registered with Restate. When wiring up the Restate SDK, this endpoint must actually implement the Restate endpoint protocol. Use the restate-sdk crate — do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol.

4. CANONICAL RESOLUTION PATH: Two paths exist for resolving a decision — the Tauri command (resolve_queue_item in project.rs, UI-driven) and the HTTP endpoint (handle_resolve_item in queue_service.rs, external/Restate-driven). In the Restate-driven future, resolution flows through Restate which calls the HTTP handler. The Tauri command becomes a thin wrapper that posts to the HTTP handler rather than duplicating logic. Establish this contract clearly in the implementation.

title: POE: Fan-in orchestration for sub-workflows
description: Parent workflow completion should be gated on all child workflows finishing. Currently children are fire-and-forget. Need: track child workflow IDs in the parent workflow record, poll or event-drive child completion, roll up status (partial failure → raise queue item asking human to retry/skip/abort), update parent node status only when all children complete.
close_reason: Implemented: schema v4 adds parent_workflow_id + child_workflow_ids columns; DagStore gets add_child_workflow/get_child_workflow_ids/get_workflow_status; fan-in check on poe:done and crash path; queue item raised on child failure

title: POE: Agent heartbeat and liveness monitoring
description: No periodic liveness check exists — only EOF-based crash detection. Need a watchdog thread that tracks last_output_at per agent and emits workflow:status=blocked if no output for N seconds. Should raise a queue item when an agent goes silent, allowing human to wait, redirect, or kill. Configurable timeout per workflow type.
close_reason: Implemented: AgentHandle tracks last_output_at + silence_alerted; watchdog tokio task polls every 30s, emits workflow:status=blocked and creates queue item after 120s of silence

title: POE Phase 5: Workflow Engine Hardening
description: Complete the workflow engine with fan-in orchestration, true Restate durable execution, agent heartbeat monitoring, and poe:decision awakeable wiring. Phase 3 built the core state machine; Phase 5 makes it production-grade.
